data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The precise distinction is scope of constraint: safe forbids intended side effects in a single call; idempotent permits side effects but requires repeated identical calls to converge to the same intended effect. For an append-only event log, readers/replayers must be safe (no mutation during replay) and writers must be idempotent; requiring writers to be safe would forbid the append itself.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If replay mutates durable state as a side effect of folding, the readers-as-safe assumption fails and the distinction collapses.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Separate read and write paths: replay reads the log and folds state with no side effects, while a writer accepts at-least-once redelivery and deduplicates by id.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
